ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all proposed partners, general partners and beneficial owners against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) list, the Criminal Code schedule, Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under SEMA, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the RCMP's Specialized Policing Services lists, and the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) SDN list where cross-border USD or US-linked payment rails (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing) are used; Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) including domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of state, senior politicians, judges, military officers, and immediate family members must undergo enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and any domestic PEP in a position of influence requiring senior-management approval; the EdTech subscription model is classified as Low_Risk_Standard but must still complete a written FINTRAC-compliant risk assessment covering the partnership, its US and international subscribers, and its digital payment processors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) portal administered by Corporations Canada / ISED; supplemented by the provincial limited partnership registry portal of the intended filing province (e.g., Ontario's Online Registration and Business Information System (ONBIS) at ontario.ca; British Columbia Corporate Online at corporateonline.gov.bc.ca; Alberta Corporate Registry at albertacorporateregistry.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Canada's federal official-languages doctrine requires that a federally-registered entity's name be usable in both English and French without linguistic conflict; for provincially-created limited partnerships registered under provincial law, the name may be in English, in French, or bilingually, and where a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese) is proposed, a mandatory English and/or French transliteration must satisfy linguistic acceptability rules; the name must not be confusingly similar to an existing federal or provincial trademark or corporate/partnership name; the legal element for a limited partnership must be Limited, Limitée, L.P., L.Tée, or the French and English equivalents
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Corporation (when the entity is not a corporation)
Limited (when used as a suffix on a non-corporate entity without the LP element)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives an official name-refusal notice from the relevant registrar (federal or provincial) stating the statutory ground (e.g., s. 12 Canada Business Corporations Act or the analogous provincial name-regulation provision); within 30 days of the refusal the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration request with the Director of Corporations Canada or the provincial Director, attaching the NUANS report, trademark search evidence, and a factual submission distinguishing the proposed name; if the administrative reconsideration is denied, a further judicial review application may be made to the Federal Court (for federal filings) or the applicable provincial superior court (for provincial LP filings), normally within 30 days of the reconsideration denial; an extended NUANS reservation or a new name search may also be purchased for CAD 13.80 to CAD 23.50 per additional search while the appeal is pending, and legal counsel typically coordinates the resubmission within the 90-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited partnerships must maintain at all times a registered office situated in the province of creation at a physical address capable of accepting service of process and official correspondence; a commercial virtual-office arrangement is permissible only where the service provider maintains a real, non-PO-box physical registered-office address, staffed access during normal business hours, and a legal-retention undertaking; a purely telecom-based virtual office with no physical service address will not satisfy Canadian registered-office requirements; the EdTech subscription business may operate with fully remote premises provided the registered office address and the provincial extra-provincial registration requirements are met
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, quantified at less than 5% annually; the Canada Revenue Agency and provincial registrars are unlikely to conduct an unannounced physical site inspection for a federally-related limited partnership engaged purely in interactive language education and automated tutoring software subscriptions; CRA compliance verification for pass-through partnerships is document-centric, and an unannounced visit would only reasonably arise upon a red-flag audit trigger (e.g., unpaid source deductions, financial integrity concerns, or FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting)

L.16, ss. 2, 7, 9; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (federal partnership tax treatment and Business Number registration)

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form 1 under R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 732)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; partners may contribute cash or in-kind. No escrow account is required by statute; capital proceeds should be deposited to the partnership bank account and fully traceable to the executed subscription schedules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Limited Partnership has received subscriptions for Partnership Interests from each proposed Limited Partner and the General Partner; RESOLVED: 1. The capital contribution and subscription schedules in the Limited Partnership Agreement are approved and accepted. 2. The Partnership's registered office is established at the address stated in the Declaration of Registration, and the General Partner is authorized to execute all necessary documents. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer and [Name] is appointed Commercial Manager, with authority to open bank accounts, sign regulatory filings, and bind the Partnership within approved limits. 4. All previous formation actions are ratified. This resolution takes effect upon statutory filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario Companies and Partnerships Branch; licensed NUANS search provider; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a name search report from a licensed search house. Check the NUANS database for corporate and trademark conflicts, confirm no prohibited or confusing name under Ontario law, and file any required name reservation to hold the proposed name while the Declaration is prepared.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to conflict, submit written consent from the prior name holder, amend the proposed name, or reserve an alternate name and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel for the General Partner; no government filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement, including capital contribution obligations, allocation ratios, withdrawal terms, and subscription acceptance. Each limited partner must execute a subscription instrument and the schedule must identify the General Partner and registered office.
required_dossiers: Register of partners and capital contributions
Consent of General Partner to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscription schedule is incomplete or amended before registration, re-execute and re-date the schedule; all partners must initial the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario Companies and Partnerships Branch (Registrar under the Limited Partnerships Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and verify Form 1 Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership, have all general partners sign, and file online or by counter with the prescribed fee. The registered office must be a physical address in Ontario; include the name search report or reservation confirmation.
required_dossiers: Name search report or reservation confirmation
Registered office address and consent of occupier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of defective filing, amend the Declaration and refile within 30 days; late corrections may require a new signature date and revised fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and tax account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the partnership for a Business Number using the CRA online service. Select partnership as the legal type, provide the certificate of limited partnership and General Partner details, register GST/HST once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and open a payroll account if employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Certificate or Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA returns a clarification request, respond through the online business account or submit an amended RC1; any delay in response may suspend GST/HST account activation but will not invalidate the partnership registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial registries where the partnership carries on business; Corporations Canada for federal cross-provincial name/entity coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Declaration, file the required extra-provincial registration in each province with a physical place of business. Provide a certified copy of the Declaration and a power of attorney designating a local attorney for service when required. Maintain one extra-provincial file per province.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for service, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a province rejects the application for incomplete certification, arrange notarization or apostille as applicable and refile; any substantive change to the partnership must be reflected in amended extra-provincial filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance records and banking account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institution chosen by the General Partner; registered office records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account in the exact legal name; provide the Declaration, Business Number, and signed resolution confirming authorized signatories. Establish a registered office file containing copies of the LP Agreement, names and addresses of partners, officer appointments, and consents.
required_dossiers: Certificate or Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC, provide source-of-funds evidence for the capital contributions and updated partner register; refusal is cured by submitting the General Partner's tax identification and entity chart.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit required for an EdTech subscription service with no physical production facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC); Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt—no physical construction, manufacturing operation, or point-source discharge; EIA screening is not triggered by software development, cloud hosting, or language-learning content delivery
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the current digital-only business model. If hardware prototyping or battery-containing devices are later introduced, applicable O. Reg. 419/05 air emissions and O. Reg. 347/02 hazardous waste thresholds will be assessed at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the industrial operations context. The registered office must comply with the Ontario Fire Code and local building occupancy permits; no structural load inspection or workplace hazardous material clearance is required for normal administrative EdTech offices. Employee workplace safety orientation under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1 is recommended.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Federal tax administration; portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html) and GST/HST NETFILE; federal business registration via Canada Business Registration (https://www.canada.ca/business-registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Limited Partnership (in Canada, governed by provincial LP statutes but federally registered) obtains a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA using Form RC1 ('Request for a Business Number') or the online Canada Business Registration service. The LP then opens a GST/HST account (program account 'RT') once taxable worldwide sales equal or exceed C$30,000 in a calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident partners without a Canadian permanent establishment must file Form RC59 (Business Number Request — Non-Resident) and may be required to file a T5013 Partnership Information Return. The BN serves as the federal tax identification number for income tax, GST/HST, customs, and payroll accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a Canadian Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for federal income tax purposes: the partnership itself is generally not subject to federal income tax, and income/losses are allocated to, and taxed at the partner level; the LP files an information return (T5013) and non-resident partners may be subject to Canadian tax under Part I (s.2(3) ITA) on Canadian-source income or Part XIII withholding on certain payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' entity classification election exists in Canada. Available statutory elections include: (i) Income Tax Act s.103 allocation election to vary partnership income/loss sharing ratios (with CRA concurrence); (ii) s.152(4) waiver of reassessment limitation period; (iii) Excise Tax Act s.156/156.2 elections for closely related corporations/partnerships for nil-consideration GST/HST supplies; (iv) s.150(2) ITA election for non-resident partners to file taxable Canadian income on a net basis; (v) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss.18.2/18.4 which are mandatory — no elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — federal GST administered by the CRA; Harmonized Sales Tax in participating provinces (e.g., Ontario 13%, Nova Scotia 15%) is a combined federal-provincial levy, but the federal component remains 5%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 in worldwide gross annual revenue from taxable supplies (including 'cross-border digital supplies' such as EdTech subscriptions made to persons resident in Canada); non-resident suppliers above this threshold (measured on a quarterly basis over four consecutive calendar quarters) are required to register for GST/HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is imposed at the federal level in Canada. Taxpayers who exceed C$1.5 million in annual taxable revenue must file GST/HST returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE); retention of electronic records is mandatory. Participation in the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing standard (PEPPOL-based, interoperable with EU regimes) is voluntary, not a clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated exports under the Excise Tax Act Schedule VI (Part V for goods; s.23 for services) and Part IX (s.21/22 transitional rules): the supplier must demonstrate that (a) the supply is made to a non-resident recipient, (b) the supply is not acquired for consumption/use in Canada, and (c) for digital EdTech subscription services (SaaS/automated tutoring), the recipient's ordinary place of residence and payment jurisdiction establish a non-Canadian place of supply; payments routed via Apple IAP / Google Play Billing to Canadian platform providers must segregate non-resident buyers and retain geo-location/payment evidence to sustain zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (G13/G13A) or e-manifest via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / electronic delivery proof for physical goods (not applicable to digital-only EdTech supplies)
Commercial Invoice and underlying subscription/software license agreement
Non-resident recipient evidence: IP address, billing country, bank/payment processor reports (Apple IAP / Google Play settlement statements)
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency receipt evidence from the recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA actively scrutinizes zero-rating claims through the GST/HST Export Verification and Refund Integrity programs. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger: (i) full assessment of unreported GST/HST plus compound interest under ETA; (ii) penalties under ETA s.285(1) for false statements — the greater of C$250 and 10% of the tax sought to be avoided; (iii) gross negligence penalties up to 50% of the deficiency where the claim was made knowingly or with willful blindness; (iv) retrospective reassessment beyond the normal four-year statutory period where misrepresentation or fraud is established; and (v) potential criminal prosecution under the Criminal Code for fraudulent refund claims, with clawbacks of input tax credits and denial of future zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with Canadian foreign exchange policy jointly administered by the Department of Finance; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) supervises AML/ATF obligations, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates federally chartered banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and OECD Liberalisation Codes; no statutory exchange controls restrict conversion of CAD, inbound capital, or outward profit repatriation. A Canadian Limited Partnership may remit profits and capital to non-resident partners without FX authorisation; however, Part I tax on Canadian-source allocated income, Part XIV branch tax on allocated income of non-resident corporate partners, and Part XIII withholding on certain passive payments may apply, with domestic rates commonly reduced by applicable tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding-period restriction on export receipts or foreign-currency revenues. Exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts without reporting to the Bank of Canada; only statistical reporting to Statistics Canada under Balance of Payments or Foreign Trade surveys may apply above prescribed thresholds, and FINTRAC large-transaction reporting applies to CAD 10,000-or-more wire transfers.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada does not issue an 'electronic money institution' licence, but non-bank payment service providers must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) before performing retail payment clearing, settlement, or payment-account functions for Canadians. A foreign digital EMI may offer cross-border collections and disbursements as a FINTRAC-registered money service business, yet such an account does not qualify as a Canadian deposit account and is unsuitable for capital escrow, debt-covenant cash balances, or long-term treasury concentration. Use of licensed payment corridors (e.g., Wise, Convera) is operationally viable for small-value subscription disbursements but must not replace a Schedule I banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person onboarding is the default standard: at least one general partner or authorised signatory must attend a branch interview and present two valid government-issued identification documents for a newly formed Limited Partnership without an existing Canadian banking relationship. Selected Schedule I banks permit remote video-verification where the beneficial ownership chain is transparent and a notarised or bank-certified identity attestation is co-signed by a Canadian-licensed lawyer or CPA; for non-resident general partners, physical attendance or a sworn Canadian professional guarantor attestation is generally required at the bank's AML discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or layered beneficial ownership, nominee limited partners, or unregistered partnership interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current partnership register, chain-of-title organisational chart, beneficial ownership declaration naming every individual holding 25% or more, certified copies of government-issued IDs, the LP declaration/registration certificate, and a notarised undertaking confirming the absence of bearer interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners or funding sources connected with high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements, recent bank reference letters from the remitting institutions, corporate tax residence certificates for all partners, completed sanctions-screening results, and a written commercial-purpose memorandum explaining the investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EdTech subscription receipts routed through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, creating a merchant-of-record chain that obscures end customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant agreements with Apple and Google, consolidated settlement statements, sub-merchant registration data, projected monthly transaction volumes and refund rates, and PCI DSS compliance attestation from the payment processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity with low average ticket size, characteristic of digital consumer subscriptions and flagged as unusual cash-flow velocity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Revenue-model documentation, historical payment-rail reports from Apple/Google, chargeback and refund policies, and accounting system extracts evidencing daily, traceable settlements to the LP's operating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate existence records, including absence of registered capital, neglected annual filings, or lack of accounting records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provincial LP registration certificate, declaration/articles of partnership, current annual return filings, registered-office address confirmation, and the engagement letter of a Canadian CPA or tax advisor confirming the ongoing accounting and tax compliance framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions must be received exclusively through identified bank-channel transfers: SWIFT MT103 wires from the contributing partner's account to the LP's segregated operational or escrow account at a Schedule I Canadian bank, using Field 70 narrative 'LP Capital Contribution' and an OECD/SWIFT purpose description consistent with direct investment (e.g., EQUI). The receiving bank applies PCMLTFA know-your-client checks and must file a Large Transaction Record with FINTRAC for any transfer of CAD 10,000 or more; the compliance file should include the partnership agreement, the capital-call notice, and partner source-of-wealth confirmation. CAD/USD conversion of inbound funds is executed at the clearing bank's intraday market rate or a pre-negotiated corporate conversion rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard supplier and trade payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers; documentary trade transactions use commercial letters of credit issued through MT700 (with MT720 and MT740 for amendments and reimbursement as applicable). CAD settlement clears through Lynx using CDSX, while USD-denominated disbursements clear via the U.S. Fedwire or CHIPS corridors at Canadian bank U.S. correspondents. All outbound wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reported to FINTRAC and must be supported by invoices, executed contracts, and sanctions-screening clearances; EdTech licensing fees, content-acquisition costs, and Apple/Google processing fees should be categorised under clearly descriptive payment narratives to avoid documentary holds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and other G10 pairs) with licensed Canadian Schedule I banks or their authorised broker-dealer affiliates
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY/CCS) for term-matched balance-sheet hedging of USD-denominated capital contributions or intercompany loans
Vanilla foreign-currency put and call options on CAD and USD pairs for premium-bounded revenue protection

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only for illiquid exotic settlement currencies lacking an onshore deliverable market; CAD itself has a fully deliverable onshore interbank market, so CAD NDFs are neither necessary nor standard

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Income Tax Act, Form T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), relevant Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after partnership fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due June 15 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of C$25 per day, minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500; additional penalties and interest apply for gross negligence, repeated non-filing, or failure to provide partner-level allocations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Registry Renewal / Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) and/or provincial corporate registry (e.g., ServiceOntario for Ontario extra-provincial LP registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of initial extra-provincial registration; filing required no later than the registration anniversary date, with provincial grace periods not exceeding 30 days in most provinces.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial late fees accrue (typically C$50–C$120); continued non-renewal leads to administrative revocation of extra-provincial registration and possible personal liability of the general partner for obligations incurred after strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (Form GST34) for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end for annual filers; monthly filers file one month after month-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file penalty equal to 5% of unremitted tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (maximum 17%); interest at prescribed CRA rates applies on balances due.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no mandatory annual independent audit for a Canadian limited partnership solely by reason of its status as an LP. A statutory audit is required when the partnership agreement mandates one, when limited partners holding at least 10% of partnership interests request an audit, or when ordered by a court or provincial securities regulator. If the LP is considered a 'large supplier' for GST/HST or carries on registrable activity in a province, the CRA may require audited financial statements during reassessment or verification proceedings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Canada for publicly accountable enterprises; for private limited partnerships, Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) in Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook apply unless the partners elect IFRS. EdTech subscription revenue is recognized under IFRS 15 / ASPE Section 3400.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a limited partnership, 'share transfers' are recorded as transfers of limited partnership interests. Annual confirmation at the federal level is not yet mandated for beneficial ownership of LPs under the current CBCA beneficial ownership regime; however, provincial registries increasingly require an annual declaration confirming the general partner, registered office, and list of limited partners. Each transfer or redemption of a limited partnership interest must be documented in the partner register and, where applicable, filed as an amendment to the extra-provincial registration. Individuals with significant control over the general partner corporation may need to be disclosed to the provincial registry where legislation (e.g., Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario) is in force.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (names, addresses, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios)
Register of General Partners and Registered Office Address
Partnership Minute Book with partner consent resolutions and amendments to the limited partnership agreement

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250 – $800 (CAD 340 – CAD 1,100) per annum depending on province and scope of registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,000 – $15,000 (CAD 8,000 – CAD 20,000) for a full financial statement audit of a mid-size EdTech limited partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate rate 15%; combined federal+provincial (Ontario example) 25.0% — applicable to corporate partners/GP of the CA LP; the LP itself is fiscally transparent
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED refundable ITC 35% for CCPCs (first C$3M qualified expenditure) / 15% non-refundable for other corporations; CCPC small business deduction 9% federal on first C$500,000 active business income allocated through the LP; no federal patent box; net capital losses offset only capital gains. For MNE groups ≥EUR 750M global revenue, Global Minimum Tax (Pillar 2) 15% effective for fiscal years beginning on/after 31 Dec 2024.
